title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-07-01
content:
Serving Runtime — weekly update (kernel work, KV cache, batching)
Week: 2026-06-29 — 2026-07-03
Author: Asha Patel (eng-serving-runtime)
Summary:
- Focus this week: finalize kernel selection logic for FP8 path, stabilize KV prefix cache eviction heuristics, and land the new continuous-batching scheduler for low-latency short requests.
- Overall goal: reduce 95th percentile latency on short-chat workloads by 15% while maintaining throughput for long-sequence workloads.
Key outcomes / wins:
- Kernel work: landed the FP8 matmul microkernel switch for 8xA100 nodes (PR #389). Initial internal benchmark shows 8–12% improvement in token throughput for decoder-only models at sequence lengths > 512. Nightly regression harness (Miguel) showed no correctness regressions on our model suite.
- KV cache: implemented a soft-eviction policy that prioritizes requests with hot-prefix hits and avoids aggressive global purge during autoscale events. In a synthetic workload we saw a ~22% increase in cache hit rate and a 7% latency improvement for second-token policy.
- Batching: experimental continuous-batching scheduler rolled out to a single pool (eu-west-1, small pool) — observed 9% increase in tokens/sec and <3ms added queuing latency for median requests.
Details / Notes:
1) Kernel selection and FP8 path
   - What we changed: new kernel selector uses a two-stage decision: (1) cost model per op (matmul, attention) computed from nightly profiling, (2) runtime fallback checks (available memory, sequence length threshold).
   - Observations: FP8 matmul gives best gains when kv-cache size is small per replica (short requests). For long contexts (>1024) FP8 needs careful dequantization to avoid quality drift — flagged to ML team for eval.
   - Open items: add a quick runtime check to disable FP8 for sequence lengths > 2048. Action: Miguel to draft change by 2026-07-07 (JIRA RT-848).
2) KV cache heuristics
   - New soft-eviction: we now track per-prefix access frequency and use a time-weighted score to evict. During scale-down events we avoid evicting prefixes with high recent reuse.
   - Metrics: synthetic replay (customer-like) shows hot-prefix hit rate improved from 61% -> 74%. Token-level latency 95p reduced from 142ms -> 131ms on small pool.
   - Issues: some tenants with highly bursty patterns still see transient misses after autoscale. Plan: add prefetch-on-scale heuristics (fetch most-recent prefixes for top-k tenants). Noah to prototype prefetch design next sprint.
3) Batching and scheduler
   - Continuous-batching scheduler: maintains a small adaptive buffer window (default 2–6ms) and uses token-cost-based admission to avoid combining very expensive requests with cheap ones.
   - Tradeoffs: good for throughput but increases tail latency when traffic is very spiky. We added a fast-path bypass for requests tagged low-latency (internal flag).
   - Rollout plan: staged to 3 pools next week, monitor token throughput and P95. If P95 increases >5% revert for pool.
4) Reliability and SRE notes
   - Observability: added tracing tags for kernel decision & cache-eviction reason. These show up in Console under the new "runtime-decisions" trace group. Useful for debugging customer regressions.
   - Incident: transient OOM on eu-west-1 small pool during kernel switch test — due to missing guard for combined attention + matmul scratch in FP8 path. Fix landed; rolling restart completed. Root cause documented in CONFLUENCE-ServingRuntime-KVCache.
Standup / meeting log (high level):
- Mon 2026-06-29: sync — kernel perf numbers, agreed to gate FP8 for very long sequences.
- Tue 2026-06-30: kv-cache design review — accepted soft-eviction, asked for prefetch proposal.
- Wed 2026-07-01: batch scheduler demo — positive signals, agreed to limited rollout.
- Thu 2026-07-02: incident postmortem and hotfix rollout.
- Fri 2026-07-03: retro and next sprint planning.
Blockers / Risks:
- FP8 model-quality risk: ML evals pending for a subset of models; if quality degrades we need to revert kernel or add per-model opt-outs.
- Autoscale prefetch complexity: prefetching prefixes across tenants can increase memory pressure; need an LRU cap + tenant-priority rules.
- Metrics drift: some of our benchmark harnesses are underestimating tail latency under real customer mixes. Working with Observability to update scenarios.
Action items (owners and ETA):
- Miguel Torres: add runtime disable for FP8 when seq_len > 2048 (by 2026-07-07) — JIRA RT-848.
- Noah Kim: prototype prefetch-on-scale and memory cap scheme (by end of sprint 2026-07-10).
- Emma Liu: extend nightly regression to include quality checks for FP8 quant/dequant (by 2026-07-08).
- Ravi Desai: rollout continuous-batching scheduler to pools eu-west-1-b and us-west-2-a (staged) and monitor P95 (start 2026-07-05).
- Asha (author): update Console dashboard to surface kernel-decision metrics and eviction reasons (by 2026-07-09).
Notes to self / team reminders:
- Keep PRs small (kernel selector + kernel impl + trace tags as separate PRs).
- Coordinate release windows with SRE — avoid rolling kernel switch during peak customer-EU morning 09:30–11:30 UTC.
- Document FP8 known limitations in the public model catalog entry so customers can opt-out if they see regressions.
Related links / references:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/389
- Design doc: CONFLUENCE-ServingRuntime-KVCache
- Incident: CONFLUENCE-ServingRuntime-Kernel-Scratch-OOM
- Jira epic: JIRA-RT-842 (kernel & kv work)
Closing thought:
We made steady progress this week — the combination of kernel tweaks and smarter KV heuristics is promising for short-chat workloads (our biggest latency-sensitive segment). The priority next week is to finish the safety gates for FP8 and validate quality across the model suite so we can flip the default for eligible pools.
